tools.name: rag.query
tools.description: Flat Vector RAG — retrieves the most relevant graph nodes by pure vector similarity (HNSW + RRF fusion + keyword fallback), then calls the configured LLM to generate a grounded answer.  Fastest of the three RAG modes (p50 ~45 ms, MRR 0.64); best for single-hop factual questions.  Use rag.graph_query or rag.hybrid_query for multi-hop or relationship-heavy questions.

tools.name: rag.graph_query
tools.description: Graph-native RAG — seeds the search with vector-nearest nodes, then expands a multi-hop BFS subgraph and builds a relationship-rich context before LLM generation.  MRR 0.76, multi-hop accuracy 0.79.  ~4x slower than flat RAG (p50 ~180 ms).  Use rag.hybrid_query for best accuracy.

seed_k.description: Number of vector-nearest seed nodes (1-20).  Default 5.

max_nodes.description: Maximum subgraph nodes in context (5-200).  Default 50.

write_inferred.description: Persist LLM-inferred edges back to the graph.  Default false.

label_filter.description: Restrict retrieval to nodes with these labels.

tools.name: rag.hybrid_query
tools.description: Hybrid Graph-Vector RAG — fuses vector similarity AND graph structural signals at every stage: dual-seed fusion (Weighted RRF over vector rank + degree centrality), vector-guided BFS, and semantic path scoring.  Highest accuracy: MRR 0.85, multi-hop 0.91.  ~5x slower (p50 ~240 ms).  Recommended as the default RAG tool for agents that need high quality.

mode.description: Fusion mode.  'balanced' for most questions; 'graph_first' for dense-relationship queries; 'vector_first' for semantic similarity.

fusion_alpha.description: Explicit graph weight (0.0=pure vector, 1.0=pure graph).  Overrides mode.

max_nodes.description: Maximum subgraph nodes in context (5-200).  Default 50.

write_inferred.description: Persist LLM-inferred edges back to the graph.  Default false.

vector_expansion.description: Filter BFS neighbours by cosine similarity.  Default true.

semantic_path_scoring.description: Rank paths by keyword overlap + edge-type bonuses.  Default true.

label_filter.description: Restrict retrieval to nodes with these labels.

collection_profile.description: Name of a saved CollectionProfile (from rag.tune_collection save_as).  Fills in mode/fusion_alpha/max_hops/seed_k as defaults — explicit params always win.

tools.name: rag.profile_collection
tools.description: Analyse the graph topology and return recommended RAG retrieval settings.  Profiles node count, edge density, degree distribution, edge-type distribution, and embedding coverage, then derives concrete values for fusion_alpha, max_hops, seed_k, vector_weight, k, and mode.  Call this before tuning rag.hybrid_query on a new corpus or collection.  Returns topology_class (sparse/moderate/dense), a 'recommended' param block ready to pass to rag.hybrid_query, and a 'rationale' explaining each choice.

label_filter.description: Restrict analysis to nodes with these labels.  Omit for whole graph.

tools.name: rag.tune_collection
tools.description: Grid-search hybrid RAG retrieval parameters against a small eval set and return the best-performing configuration.  Runs profile_collection() to derive a topology-aware baseline, then evaluates combinations of fusion_alpha / expand_hops / seed_k using token-F1 between retrieved context and expected answers (retrieval-only mode — no LLM generation).  Returns best_params, best_score, baseline_score, improvement_pct, and full grid_results.  Requires an LLM provider configured (embedding step only).  Call after rag.profile_collection when you want autonomous param optimisation or when retrieval quality has degraded due to corpus drift.

eval_set.description: 5–20 question/expected_answer pairs to evaluate retrieval quality.

label_filter.description: Restrict tuning to nodes with these labels.  Omit for whole graph.

max_iterations.description: Maximum number of param combinations to evaluate.  Default 12.

save_as.description: If provided, persist best_params as a named CollectionProfile after tuning.  Pass this name to rag.hybrid_query collection_profile to auto-apply the optimal params on every subsequent query — zero manual config required.

tools.name: graph.query
tools.description: Execute a Cypher query against the Purple8 knowledge graph and return matching records.  Use for nodes, edges, paths, or aggregated data.

tools.name: graph.vector_search
tools.description: Find the k nearest nodes to a natural-language query using the HNSW vector index.

query_text.description: The search query in natural language.

label.description: Restrict search to nodes with this label.

k.description: Number of results to return.  Default 5.

tools.name: graph.hybrid_search
tools.description: Combine vector similarity with graph traversal for highest-recall retrieval.  Best when graph structure matters.

query_text.description: The search query in natural language.

label.description: Restrict search to nodes with this label.

k.description: Number of results to return.  Default 10.

tools.name: graph.traverse
tools.description: Walk the graph from a starting node following edges up to a given depth.

edge_type.description: Restrict to edges of this type.  Omit for all types.

tools.name: graph.add_node
tools.description: Insert a new node into the graph (accepts `type`, `label`, or `node_type`).  Requires editor role.

tools.name: graph.add_edge
tools.description: Create a directed edge (relationship) between two existing nodes.  This is the primary agentic handoff mechanism — agents write their output as edges (e.g. DERIVED_FROM, RISK_ASSESSMENT, EXTRACTED_FROM) so downstream agents can discover work by querying graph state rather than passing messages.  edge_id is auto-generated (UUID4) when omitted.  Requires editor role.

edge_id.description: Unique identifier for the edge.  Auto-generated UUID4 when omitted.

weight.description: Edge weight for traversal algorithms.  Default 1.0.

tools.name: graph.update_node
tools.description: Update properties or labels on an existing node.  Properties are merged with existing values (patch semantics — only the keys you supply are changed).  Labels replace the full label set when provided.  Use this to advance agent relay state, e.g. setting {"status": "enriched", "handoff_to": null} to hand off work to the next agent in a relay pipeline.  Requires editor role.

node_id.description: ID of the node to update.

properties.description: Properties to merge into the node (patch semantics).

labels.description: Replacement label set (replaces all existing labels when provided).

tools.name: graph.get_node
tools.description: Retrieve a node and all its stored properties by ID.

node_id.description: ID of the node to retrieve.

tools.name: graph.pagerank
tools.description: Run PageRank on the graph and return the top-ranked (most influential) nodes.

label.description: Restrict PageRank to nodes with this label.

top_k.description: Number of top nodes to return.  Default 20.

tools.name: graph.communities
tools.description: Detect communities (Louvain) in the graph.  Useful for discovering entity clusters.

label.description: Restrict community detection to nodes with this label.

tools.name: data.ingest_text
tools.description: Extract entities and relationships from raw text and write them into the graph. Calls preview first, then commits the complete extraction on success. auto_commit=false returns a review-only preview. Pending jobs return job_id for resumption. Original bytes are not stored automatically; supply file_ref or use data.commit with file_bytes_b64 if needed. After an interrupted write, ask the user to confirm a retry; use data.commit with the retained reviewed payload instead of re-extracting. Requires editor role.

text.description: The raw text to extract knowledge from.

auto_commit.description: false returns the complete preview without graph writes. Review then use data.commit.

job_id.description: Resume an earlier extraction instead of submitting again; repeat the original input arguments.

wait_seconds.description: Maximum wait for an admitted extraction. Pending jobs are NOT committed; resume with job_id.

file_ref.description: Optional existing Graph file_id in this tenant, used as the original/document anchor at commit.

tools.name: data.commit
tools.description: Commit a reviewed extraction or your own extractor's output without invoking DocIntel. Uses the complete POST /ingest/commit contract: entities, relationships, Markdown, spans, tables/pages, context, file_ref or inline file_bytes_b64 and ingestion options. Existing entities are linked, not edited, unless update_entities=true. For extractor-generated IDs use identity_policy='review_conflicts': name matches alone are not identity proof. On entity_identity_conflict nothing was written; correct/exclude the incoming entity and update relationship endpoints, or explicitly confirm identity_resolution='link_existing', then retry. link_existing never edits existing facts. After interruption or a lost response, ask the user to confirm retrying the retained reviewed payload. Reuse entity IDs, assertion keys and file_ref; do not automatically re-extract. Retain metadata.sha256 (original bytes) and optional metadata.file_version. On source_version_conflict nothing was written: obtain and review current-source extraction and ask for confirmation, rather than replaying or relabeling the old review. SIMILAR_TO edges (enabled by default) are similarity, not factual assertions. Inspect embedding, document_chunks, structured_content and original_file outcomes; a successful write alone does not guarantee retrieval readiness. Requires editor role.

CommitPage.description: A page/slide/sheet as a ``[char_start, char_end)`` range of ``markdown``.
CommitPage.title: CommitPage

CommitTable.description: A document table as rows (``[row][col]`` strings, header rows first).
CommitTable.title: CommitTable

DocumentContextClaims.description:
Content-derived 4D context-signal fields — the *claim* half of the barcode.

These are extracted from the document by Purple8-DocIntel and are, by nature,
*claims* (the document asserting facts about itself), as opposed to the
engine-stamped high-trust fields (``_ctx.ingested_at`` / ``_ctx.tenant`` /
``_ctx.ingest_actor``) which the graph engine writes itself.

Every field is **optional** — the barcode degrades gracefully when a signal is
absent (missing → neutral at scoring time, never a penalty).  The ingest
router translates these to reserved ``_ctx.*`` node properties and runs
:func:`~purple8_graph.core.context_signal.validate_context_types` before
writing, so a malformed claim is rejected at the boundary rather than silently
corrupting the retrieval scorer downstream.  See ``purple8-company: ip/trade-secrets/context-signal-4d.md``.

content_time.description: Primary date the content is ABOUT (ISO-8601), e.g. '2025-09-30'.
content_time.title: Content Time

content_time_span.description: Optional [start, end] ISO-8601 range the content covers.
content_time_span.title: Content Time Span

geo.description: Locations mentioned in the content, e.g. ['London, UK'].
geo.title: Geo

author.description: Authoring entity named in the content, e.g. 'entity:JPMorgan'.
author.title: Author

doc_type_confidence.description: Confidence in the doc_type classification, in [0.0, 1.0].
doc_type_confidence.title: Doc Type Confidence

DocumentContextClaims.title: DocumentContextClaims

identity.description: Explicit stable identifiers, keyed by namespace (for example company_registration). Not inferred from arbitrary properties.
identity.title: Identity

identity_resolution.description: link_existing explicitly confirms this ID is the intended existing entity despite conflicting identity evidence; it does not request an edit.
identity_resolution.title: Identity Resolution

relation_keys.description: Shared semantic keys that trigger CO_RELEVANT edges across batches. Any two nodes with the same key will be connected automatically.
relation_keys.title: Relation Keys

identity_policy.description: review_conflicts rejects conflicting names/types/identifiers and cross-document name-only matches before writes. Supply matching stable identifiers, same-source provenance, or explicit link_existing confirmation. trust_ids preserves caller-managed ID semantics. Explicit identifier evidence is checked in either mode.
identity_policy.title: Identity Policy

metadata.description: Preserve extraction metadata. For a stored File, sha256 binds the review to original bytes (not Markdown); optional file_version pins its positive integer version. A changed/missing bound source returns source_version_conflict (409) before writes. Unpinned legacy payloads cannot prove that their review matches the current source.
metadata.title: Metadata

build_similarity_edges.description: Build SIMILAR_TO edges to cross-batch neighbours via vector search. On by default — turns every commit into a native hybrid ingest.
build_similarity_edges.title: Build Similarity Edges

similarity_threshold.description: Minimum cosine similarity for SIMILAR_TO edge creation.
similarity_threshold.title: Similarity Threshold

similarity_k.description: Number of nearest neighbours to consider per node.
similarity_k.title: Similarity K

file_id.description: Content-hash / File node ID for a file-backed commit. When provided, the orchestrator creates File → HAS_CHUNK → Chunk edges.
file_id.title: File Id

raw_text.description: Full document text used to extract per-chunk text from section_boundaries. Pass the complete text for accurate MENTIONED_IN linkage.
raw_text.title: Raw Text

upsert.description: Idempotent re-projection mode (default on): never create __vN twins, and derive deterministic edge ids so re-commits converge instead of duplicating.
upsert.title: Upsert

update_entities.description: Merge this document's values into entities that already exist. Off by default: existing entities are linked, not modified. Requires edit access to every existing entity (403 otherwise; nothing is written).
update_entities.title: Update Entities

tools.name: data.replace_file
tools.description: Upload a new version of an existing file blob. The current blob is automatically archived as v1 (idempotent). The new bytes become v{N+1}. The File node is updated (version, content_hash, blob_ref, size_bytes, updated_at). Immutable FileVersion records distinguish the previous version from the exact base. Set base_version to revise from an older version without losing intervening history. Set intent=linked_file and base_version to create an independent linked File instead. Superseded source versions and extraction records remain available as archived history. DocIntel processing is queued by default. Set re_extract=false for reviewed/custom ingestion. Use data.list_file_versions to inspect the version history afterwards. Requires editor role.

file_id.description: ID of the File node to replace (the content hash from the original upload).

url.description: Publicly accessible URL of the new file to fetch and store as the replacement.

re_extract.description: Process automatically; false defers to reviewed/custom ingestion.

base_version.description: Exact source version; required for linked_file, otherwise defaults to current.

tools.name: data.patch_file_properties
tools.description: Update mutable metadata on a File node without touching the stored blob or bumping the version number. Fields: filename, description, tags (list of strings), classification. Only the supplied fields are updated; omitted fields are left unchanged. Requires editor role.

file_id.description: ID of the File node to update.

description.description: Human-readable description of the file's content or purpose.

tools.name: data.list_file_versions
tools.description: Return the full version history of a stored file, oldest to newest. Each entry contains: version (int), filename, size_bytes, content_hash, file_ref, modified_at. If no version history exists yet (file pre-dates versioning), a synthesised v1 record is returned from the current node properties. Use GET /files/{id}/versions/{ver} to download a specific version. Requires viewer role.

file_id.description: ID of the File node to inspect.

tools.name: data.get_table
tools.description: Summary of a stored document table (from a commit with tables): columns, inferred column_types, indexed_columns (with which layer set them), typed_status / typed_skipped, and link_rules. Table ids appear in the commit response and on Table nodes. Requires viewer role.

tools.name: data.link_table_rows
tools.description: Declare rule-based links from a table's rows to entities and apply them. Each rule: column (header name), target_label (e.g. Organization), match (exact_id | name_exact | name_normalised, default name_normalised), edge (UPPER_SNAKE, default REFERS_TO), on_missing (skip | create, default skip), columns_include (optional header columns the table must have). Rules are stored on the table and re-applied on re-extraction. Re-running is idempotent; edges that no longer match are removed. replace=true drops rules not listed (and their edges). All-or-nothing. Requires editor role.

tools.name: data.index_table_columns
tools.description: Mark table columns as indexed: each row gets a typed copy (<col>__n number, __d ISO date, __b bool) next to the original string, and a property index is built scoped to that table. Set at the 'agent' layer: a column a user already set is not overridden. Cells that do not parse keep only their string and are counted in typed_skipped. Requires editor role.

tools.name: data.query_table_rows
tools.description: Filter one table's rows. 'where' maps a column to a value (equality) or to operators {$eq,$ne,$lt,$lte,$gt,$gte,$in,$nin,$exists}. Indexed typed columns compare as numbers / ISO dates / bools and operands are parsed like cells ("£1,200", "3 March 2025"); other columns compare strings. Call data.index_table_columns first to range-filter a numeric or date column. Returns rows ordered by row_index, each with its cells.

tools.name: journey.start
tools.description: Create a new Journey Engine instance for an entity and move it to the first stage.  All transitions are recorded as immutable graph edges.  Requires editor role.

entity_id.description: ID of the entity node the journey is for.

tools.name: journey.advance
tools.description: Advance a journey instance to the next stage.  Actor and notes are written to the audit trail as an ADVANCED_TO edge.  Requires editor role.

notes.description: Optional notes for the audit trail.

tools.name: journey.status
tools.description: Return the full state and audit trail for a journey instance — every stage transition, AI recommendation, and HITL decision.

tools.name: journey.define
tools.description: Define a new journey type (workflow template) with ordered stages, owner systems, and per-stage SLA policies.  Once defined, instances can be started with journey.start.  Call this first when building any new workflow — the agent can define the entire process in one call.  Use overwrite=true to update an existing definition. Requires journey:admin permission (admin or super_admin by default). Use operation=configure_ai with ai_enabled to persistently enable/disable this tenant's advisor. Generation uses tenant LLM settings; delivery is currently best-effort.

ai_enabled.description: Required for configure_ai. Explicit opt-in to automatic LLM calls for this tenant.

journey_type.description: Unique snake_case name for this workflow (e.g. 'loan_application', 'supplier_approval').

description.description: Human-readable description of what this journey tracks.

stages.description: Ordered list of stages.  First stage is the initial state.

sla_warn_seconds.description: Emit SLA warning after N seconds in this stage.  0 = no warning.

sla_breach_seconds.description: Mark instance STALLED after N seconds in this stage.  0 = no enforcement.

terminal.description: If true, reaching this stage marks the instance as completed.  Use for branching exits (e.g. 'approved' / 'rejected').

hitl.description: Human-In-The-Loop approval gate.  When set, advancing into this stage automatically creates a pending HITL task that must be resolved before the instance can continue.

required.description: Whether the approval task must be resolved before advancing.

assigned_role.description: Role that can action this task (e.g. 'compliance_officer').

title.description: Task title shown to the reviewer.

description.description: Task description / instructions for the reviewer.

advance_to_stage.description: Stage to advance to on approval.  Defaults to next stage.

expires_in_seconds.description: Optional deadline for the HITL task (seconds).  Null = no deadline.

ai_step.description: Native stage advisory configuration. Uses tenant LLM settings after configure_ai opt-in; auto_execute=false suggests only and HITL gates remain enforced.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing definition with the same journey_type.  Default false.

tools.name: journey.list
tools.description: List journey instances with optional filters.  Use this to discover what is in flight, find instances for a specific entity, or check all instances of a given type.  Also returns all defined journey types when called with no arguments.  Essential for any agent monitoring or orchestrating workflows. Set runtime_status=true to inspect this tenant's advisor enablement, provider readiness and delivery guarantees.

entity_id.description: Filter by the entity the journey is tracking.

list_types.description: Return defined journey type names instead of instances.  Default false.

runtime_status.description: Return tenant Journey AI configuration/readiness instead of instances.

tools.name: journey.sla_alerts
tools.description: Inspect and operate tenant SLA monitoring. operation=breached (default) returns active journey instances that have breached their SLA. health reports local monitor state, not scheduler/provider health. history returns a bounded event page for instance_id in event-type/native-adjacency order, not time order. acknowledge appends an immutable acknowledgement (journey:write); reset resumes only a stalled occurrence and resets its clock (journey:admin), requiring reason and expected_stage_entered_at from journey.status. Acknowledgement does not resolve a breach or change the clock. Legacy breach results contain active instances past their breach deadline. Use history for recorded warning/breach events. Use this for proactive monitoring: an agent can poll this tool on a schedule and take remediation actions (escalate, reassign, cancel) without waiting for a human to notice.

journey_type.description: Restrict to a specific journey type.  Omit for all types.

tools.name: journey.list_hitl
tools.description: List pending Human-In-The-Loop (HITL) tasks — decisions that require a human (or agent acting as human proxy) to approve, reject, or escalate before the journey can continue.  Returns task ID, title, assigned role, description, and the stage the journey is waiting on.  An agent can use this to surface pending decisions to the user or take autonomous action if authorised.

instance_id.description: Restrict to HITL tasks for a specific journey instance.

status.description: Filter by task status.  Default: pending.

tools.name: journey.resolve_hitl
tools.description: Resolve a Human-In-The-Loop (HITL) task — approve, reject, or escalate it.  On approval the journey automatically advances to the next stage if advance_to_stage is set.  The decision is written to the immutable graph audit trail with the actor and timestamp.  An AI agent acting as a human proxy must set actor to the user or role it is acting on behalf of.  Requires editor role.

task_id.description: ID of the HITL task to resolve.

actor.description: User or system making the decision (written to audit trail).

decision.description: Decision label for complete actions (e.g. 'approved', 'denied').  Default 'approved'.

advance_to_stage.description: Stage to advance the journey to on completion.  Omit to leave stage unchanged.

notes.description: Notes written to the audit trail.

new_assigned_role.description: New role to escalate to (required when action=escalate).

tools.name: journey.audit
tools.description: Retrieve the immutable audit trail for a journey instance.  Returns every stage transition, HITL decision, SLA event, and AI-step note recorded against the instance, in chronological order.  The audit trail is append-only — nothing can be deleted or mutated.  Use this to review what happened, why an instance stalled, or what an AI agent decided at each step.  Requires viewer role.

instance_id.description: Journey instance ID to retrieve the audit trail for.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return (most recent first).  0 = all.

tools.name: data.ingest_file
tools.description: Send a document file (PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, IFC, CSV, …) to Purple8 DocIntel for parsing, entity extraction, and graph ingestion.  The document is fetched by DocIntel from a public URL, not a local path. The complete extraction is committed only when finished successfully. auto_commit=false returns a review-only preview; pending jobs return job_id for resumption. URL extraction does not retain original bytes in Graph; supply file_ref or commit an original separately. Use this when the knowledge source is a document rather than raw text.  Requires editor role and DocIntel to be running. After an interrupted write, ask the user to confirm a retry; use data.commit with the retained reviewed payload instead of re-extracting.

url.description: Publicly accessible URL of the document to fetch and process.

auto_commit.description: false returns the complete preview without graph writes. Review then use data.commit.

job_id.description: Resume an earlier extraction instead of submitting again; repeat the original input arguments.

wait_seconds.description: Maximum wait for an admitted extraction. Pending jobs are NOT committed; resume with job_id.

file_ref.description: Optional existing Graph file_id in this tenant, used as the original/document anchor at commit.

tools.name: graph.poll_changes
tools.description: Poll the CDC (Change Data Capture) event stream for recent graph mutations. Returns up to *limit* events that occurred after *since_sequence* (exclusive). Use this to detect new nodes, edges, or journey transitions without a persistent connection — ideal for agents that need to react to graph changes.  Store the highest *sequence* from the response and pass it as *since_sequence* on the next poll to advance the cursor.  Start with since_sequence=0 to read from the beginning.  Filter by event_type (node_added, edge_added, node_updated, edge_updated, node_deleted, edge_deleted) to reduce noise.

since_sequence.description: Return only events with sequence > this value.  Pass 0 to start from the beginning.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return.  Default 50, max 500.

event_type.description: Filter to a specific event type: node_added, edge_added, node_updated, edge_updated, node_deleted, edge_deleted.  Omit for all types.

tools.name: graph.wait_for_changes
tools.description: Block until the next graph mutation after *since_sequence*, or until *timeout* seconds elapse — a push-latency alternative to graph.poll_changes.  Where poll_changes returns immediately (an instant snapshot), wait_for_changes holds the connection open and returns the moment a matching event occurs, so reacting agents see changes with near-zero latency and without burning CPU in a tight polling loop.  Ideal for multi-agent coordination: one agent writes to the graph, another is woken instantly to react.  Cursor semantics are identical to poll_changes — store the response *next_since_sequence* and pass it back on the next call.  The response includes a *waited* flag: false = events were already available (catch-up), true = the call blocked (and may return an empty list on timeout, which is normal — just call again to keep waiting).  Filter by event_type to be woken only by node_added, edge_added, node_updated, edge_updated, node_deleted, or edge_deleted.

since_sequence.description: Return only events with sequence > this value.  Pass 0 to start from the beginning.

timeout.description: Maximum seconds to block waiting for the first event (0–60).  0 = non-blocking catch-up only.  Default 25.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return.  Default 50, max 500.

event_type.description: Filter to a specific event type: node_added, edge_added, node_updated, edge_updated, node_deleted, edge_deleted.  Omit for all types.

tools.name: graph.auto_config
tools.description: Inspect the hardware-derived QCDR configuration recommendation for this Purple8 engine, and optionally simulate the impact of parameter overrides before committing.  Called with no arguments: returns the current proposal — hardware detected, quality tier chosen, QCDR assessment per dimension (Quality/Cost/Speed/Risk), and the five tuning levers available.  Called with one or more override parameters: runs what_if() and returns a structured diff showing exactly which QCDR dimensions improve, degrade, or stay unchanged — so you can tune with confidence before locking down.  All parameters are optional.  Example: {"M": 8} shows the QCDR impact of lowering graph connectivity.  Example: {"alpha": 0.9} shows the impact of using 90% of available RAM.

M.description: HNSW graph connectivity per node (4–32).  Higher = better recall, more RAM per segment.

ef_construction.description: ef during HNSW build (8–1024).  Higher = better recall, slower ingest.

segment_size.description: Nodes per sealed segment.  Larger = fewer segments, more RAM per seal cycle.

batch_size.description: Write-buffer batch size.  Larger = higher throughput, more peak RAM.

max_hot_segments.description: Sealed segments pinned in RAM.  Higher = lower cold-I/O risk.

alpha.description: Target RAM fraction (0.1–1.0).  Higher = more budget, higher peak RSS risk.

tools.name: graph.delete_node
tools.description: Delete a node and all its incident edges from the graph.  Returns ``{"deleted": true}`` when the node existed and was removed, or ``{"deleted": false}`` when no node with that ID was found.  Requires editor role.  For source Files set file=true to use the lineage-safe file lifecycle. Set erase=true with a documented reason for explicit erasure (super_admin only); surviving derivatives are reported for review, not silently erased. ⚠ human_only — agents are blocked; a human operator must perform this action directly.

node_id.description: ID of the node to delete.

file.description: Use the source File lifecycle, not generic node deletion.

tools.name: rag.rerank
tools.description: Graph-signal reranking of vector / hybrid search candidates.  Takes a list of ``{node_id, score, ...}`` candidates (as returned by graph.vector_search or rag.hybrid_query), blends their base cosine score with a graph-neighbourhood density signal, and returns them sorted by the combined final score.  alpha=1.0 = pure base score (no-op rerank).  alpha=0.0 = pure graph signal.  Default alpha=0.7 — strongly favours base score while rewarding hubs.

candidates.description: List of candidate objects, each with ``node_id`` (str) and ``score`` (float) fields.  Additional fields are passed through.

top_k.description: Return at most this many results.  Omit to return all.

tools.name: quantum.anneal
tools.description: Run Simulated Annealing (optionally with greedy refinement) on a QUBO problem and return the best binary solution found.  Suitable for combinatorial optimisation problems including VRP, scheduling, and binary portfolio selection.  hybrid=true (default) runs a greedy descent pass after SA which typically reduces residual energy by 2–15 %.  Requires editor role.

Q.description: n×n QUBO coupling matrix (row-major list of lists).

hybrid.description: Run greedy refinement after SA.  Default true.

tools.name: quantum.optimize
tools.description: Topology-aware QUBO solver dispatch — automatically selects between greedy descent, simulated annealing, tabu search, and hybrid SA+greedy based on problem size and density.  Prefer this over quantum.anneal when you don't need explicit solver control.  Returns the solution, energy, and the solver profile that was used.  Requires editor role.

tools.name: quantum.simulate
tools.description: Construct a random Matrix Product State (MPS) tensor network and optionally compute the expectation value ⟨ψ|O|ψ⟩ for a given MPO operator.  Useful for validating tensor network calculations without a quantum hardware backend.  operator='identity' verifies norm preservation; operator='transverse_ising' computes the Ising Hamiltonian expectation.  Requires editor role.

phys_dim.description: Physical dimension d (2 for qubits).  Default 2.

operator.description: MPO to apply.  Omit to return norm only.

tools.name: quantum.encode_state
tools.description: Encode a quantum state vector and store it as a Purple8 graph node.  The state is HNSW-indexed via an interleaved real/imag embedding so it can be retrieved by fidelity similarity or compared pair-wise via quantum.compare.  Accepts a complex amplitude vector split into real and imaginary lists.  The state is automatically normalised.  Returns the HilbertStateRecord with the assigned state_id and node_id.  Requires editor role.

metadata.description: Arbitrary key-value metadata stored on the graph node.

tools.name: quantum.measure
tools.description: Simulate projective measurement of a stored quantum state.  Loads the state vector from the graph store and samples n_shots computational-basis outcomes according to the Born-rule probability distribution.  Returns counts per bitstring and the dominant (most-probable) outcome.  Requires viewer role.

state_id.description: ID of a previously encoded state (from quantum.encode_state).

tools.name: quantum.vqe_step
tools.description: Execute one Variational Quantum Eigensolver step using a pure-numpy RBM (Restricted Boltzmann Machine) variational ansatz.  Pass the weights from the previous step to continue training; omit them to start from a random initialisation.  Returns updated weights and the estimated ground-state energy.  Loop this tool to converge toward the variational ground state.  Supports transverse_ising and heisenberg Hamiltonians.  Requires editor role.

use_sr.description: Use Stochastic Reconfiguration (natural gradient).  Default false.

weights_a.description: Visible bias weights from prior step.

weights_b.description: Hidden bias weights from prior step.

weights_W_flat.description: Flattened (n_visible×n_hidden) weight matrix from prior step.

tools.name: quantum.compare
tools.description: Compute the quantum fidelity F = |⟨ψ_A|ψ_B⟩|² between two stored quantum states.  Both states must have been previously encoded via quantum.encode_state.  Returns fidelity in [0, 1]: 1.0 = identical states, 0.0 = orthogonal.  Useful for checking whether two optimisation solutions correspond to the same quantum state, or for nearest-state retrieval workflows.  Requires viewer role.

tools.name: quantum.profile
tools.description: Recommend the optimal QUBO solver for a given problem size and density.  No computation is performed — this is a pure advisory call.  Returns the recommended solver method, an anneal config dict ready to pass to quantum.anneal, and a rationale.  Call this before quantum.optimize when you need explicit time/quality trade-off control.  Requires viewer role.

density.description: Fraction of non-zero off-diagonal entries (0.0–1.0).  Default 0.5.

tools.name: graph.import_nquads
tools.description: Import bounded RDF 1.1 N-Quads with an explicit stable blank_node_scope. Full parse and authorization preflight precede writes. Quads commit individually, not atomically; interruption reports acknowledged progress. Retry the entire input with the same scope. Requires data:import and node/edge read/create permissions. Preserves lexical literals; no URL fetching or inference.

tools.name: graph.assert_statement
tools.description: Idempotently assert one native RDF quad with exact lexical terms, explicit blank-node scope and optional graph name. Uses existing node/edge create and read permissions, record policies and API-key label restrictions. No bulk import or caller-supplied metadata.

RDFStatement.description: One asserted quad. None identifies the default graph, not every graph.
RDFStatement.title: RDFStatement

RDFTerm.description: An immutable RDF term; blank-node scope is explicit, never global.
RDFTerm.title: RDFTerm

tools.name: graph.retract_statement
tools.description: Physically remove exactly one native RDF quad, preserving other graph memberships. Admin-only; existing node/edge delete and read permissions, visibility policies and legal holds apply. human_only: AI agent callers are blocked.

RDFStatement.description: One asserted quad. None identifies the default graph, not every graph.
RDFStatement.title: RDFStatement

RDFTerm.description: An immutable RDF term; blank-node scope is explicit, never global.
RDFTerm.title: RDFTerm

tools.name: graph.semantic_query
tools.description: Read-only indexed RDF/LPG pattern query with policy-filtered evidence. Use tagged rdf, lpg and lpg_edge patterns. Returns unified bindings and evidence or, with output_format=nquads, a JSON envelope containing selected asserted N-Quads and selection metadata. Raw work stats are withheld (stats=null). No inferred RDF, writes, import, or whole-corpus export. Existing read permissions apply; N-Quads additionally requires data:export.

LPGNodeVariable.description: A tenant-local node ID binding, never an RDF term.
LPGNodeVariable.title: LPGNodeVariable

RDFTerm.description: An immutable RDF term; blank-node scope is explicit, never global.
RDFTerm.title: RDFTerm

RDFVariable.description: A shared term binding, named without a leading question mark.
RDFVariable.title: RDFVariable

SemanticQueryLimits.description: Finite per-call work and result limits; exhaustion is an error.
SemanticQueryLimits.title: SemanticQueryLimits

tools.name: graph.get_edge
tools.description: Fetch a single edge (relationship) by its edge_id, returning its type, source and target node IDs, and properties.  The edge counterpart of graph.get_node.

tools.name: graph.delete_edge
tools.description: Delete a single edge (relationship) by its edge_id.  The edge counterpart of graph.delete_node — completes graph CRUD so an agent can remove a relationship without deleting either endpoint.  ⚠ human_only — agents are blocked; a human operator must perform this action directly.

edge_id.description: The unique edge identifier to delete.

tools.name: graph.edges_exist
tools.description: Batch relationship-existence check (up to 500 pairs per call).  Given a list of directed pairs (each source_id + target_id, optional edge_type), returns which relationships already exist.  Use this before bulk edge creation to avoid duplicate relationships — the single most useful primitive for iterative graph building by an agent.

pairs.description: Up to 500 {source_id, target_id, edge_type?} objects to check.

tools.name: graph.shortest_path
tools.description: Find the shortest weighted path from one node to another (Dijkstra).  Returns the ordered node sequence and total cost, or a 404 if the target is unreachable.  A core reasoning primitive — 'how is X connected to Y'.

weight_property.description: Edge property to use as weight.  Omit for hop-count (unit weights).

edge_type.description: Restrict traversal to a single edge type.  Omit to use all edges.

tools.name: graph.morans_i
tools.description: Compute Moran's I global spatial autocorrelation statistic over a set of nodes.  Measures whether nodes with similar *value_property* cluster together (I > 0), are dispersed (I < 0), or are randomly arranged (I ≈ 0) across the adjacency graph defined by *weight_edge_type* edges.  Returns I, z-score, analytical p-value, permutation p-value, and a human-readable interpretation string.  Ideal for detecting geographic or structural clustering in knowledge graphs before running LISA (graph.local_morans_i).

weight_property.description: Edge property for weight value. Default 'weight'.

row_standardise.description: Row-standardise the spatial weights matrix. Default true.

permutations.description: Permutations for pseudo p-value (0 = analytical only). Default 999.

tools.name: graph.local_morans_i
tools.description: Compute LISA (Local Indicators of Spatial Association) for every node in the graph — the local version of Moran's I.  Classifies each node as HH (hot spot), LL (cold spot), HL or LH (spatial outlier), or NS (not significant).  Returns per-node LISA scores, cluster types, p-values, and a cluster_summary dict.  Use after graph.morans_i confirms global clustering — LISA pinpoints exactly which nodes drive the pattern.

weight_property.description: Edge property for weight value. Default 'weight'.

row_standardise.description: Row-standardise the spatial weights matrix. Default true.

permutations.description: Permutations for conditional pseudo p-value. Default 999.

tools.name: graph.centrality
tools.description: Betweenness-centrality ranking (Brandes' algorithm, exact or approximate) — the nodes that lie on the most shortest paths, i.e. the graph's structural bottlenecks / brokers.  Pass sample_size > 0 and pivot_strategy ('random' or 'degree') for O(S·E) approximate betweenness on large graphs (Phase 7.4).  Scores are normalised 0–1 by default.

top_k.description: Return the top-K most central nodes.  Default 20.

sample_size.description: Number of pivot nodes to sample for O(S·E) approximate betweenness (0 = exact Brandes).

pivot_strategy.description: Pivot selection strategy when sample_size > 0: 'random' or 'degree'.

tools.name: graph.link_prediction
tools.description: Predict likely-but-missing edges for a node using a chosen similarity method: jaccard, adamic_adar, resource_allocation, preferential_attachment, common_neighbours, or personalised_pagerank.  Returns ranked candidate target nodes with scores — directly useful for recommendation, entity resolution, and knowledge-graph completion.

node_id.description: Node to predict new links for.

method.description: jaccard | adamic_adar | resource_allocation | preferential_attachment | common_neighbours | personalised_pagerank.  Default adamic_adar.

top_k.description: Number of candidate links to return.  Default 10.

label.description: Restrict candidate targets to this label.  Omit for all.

tools.name: graph.personalised_pagerank
tools.description: Compute Personalised PageRank (PPR) rooted at a seed node (Phase 7.12).  Ranks nodes by random-walk proximity to seed_id with configurable damping alpha and max_iterations.

seed_id.description: Seed node ID to personalise PageRank around.

top_k.description: Number of top-scoring nodes to return. Default 20.

tools.name: graph.triangles
tools.description: Count triangles per node and compute local and global clustering coefficients across the graph (Phase 7.11).

tools.name: graph.bridges
tools.description: Find bridge edges whose removal disconnects the graph using iterative Tarjan DFS in O(V+E) time (Phase 7.11).  Identifies single-point-of-failure links in infrastructure, supply chains, or structural topologies.

tools.name: graph.articulation_points
tools.description: Find biconnected components and articulation points (cut vertices whose removal disconnects the graph) via Tarjan's algorithm (Phase 7.11).

tools.name: graph.bipartite_check
tools.description: Determine whether the graph (or a pair of node labels) is bipartite via BFS 2-colouring and return the two partitions (Phase 7.11).

tools.name: graph.bipartite_matching
tools.description: Compute maximum cardinality bipartite matching between two node label partitions via Hopcroft-Karp in O(E √V) (Phase 7.11).

label_a.description: Label of nodes in partition A.

label_b.description: Label of nodes in partition B.

tools.name: graph.mst
tools.description: Compute the Minimum Spanning Tree / Forest using Kruskal's algorithm + union-find (Phase 7.11).

weight_property.description: Edge property to use as weight. Omit for edge.weight.

tools.name: graph.motifs
tools.description: Count directed 3-node triad motif patterns (feed-forward loops, cycles, mutual dyads, etc.) in the graph (Phase 7.11).

tools.name: graph.temporal_pagerank
tools.description: Compute PageRank with exponential recency decay exp(-λ × age) on edge timestamps so recent relationships carry higher authority (Phase 7.3).

reference_time.description: ISO-8601 reference timestamp. Omit for current UTC time.

tools.name: graph.dynamic_pagerank
tools.description: Incremental PageRank update after edge additions or removals (Phase 7.3).  Re-scores only the k-hop frontier of changed edges instead of recomputing the entire graph.

added_edges.description: List of [source_id, target_id] pairs added since last run.

removed_edges.description: List of [source_id, target_id] pairs removed since last run.

tools.name: graph.dynamic_communities
tools.description: Incremental community detection after edge additions or removals (Phase 7.3).  Re-runs label propagation only on the 2-hop neighbourhood of affected nodes.

tools.name: graph.structural_roles
tools.description: Fingerprint nodes into structural role classes using logarithmic degree bins and clustering-coefficient bins (Phase 7.4).

tools.name: graph.rolesim
tools.description: Find nodes with the highest structural role similarity to a query node (Phase 7.4 RoleSim) — identifies structurally equivalent brokers, hubs, or leaves even when they share no neighbours.

tools.name: graph.fraud_rings
tools.description: Detect dense-subgraph communities likely to represent collusive fraud rings (Phase 7.5).  Runs label propagation and returns communities whose internal edge density ≥ min_density.

min_ring_size.description: Minimum nodes in a ring. Default 3.

tools.name: graph.simrank
tools.description: Compute SimRank structural similarity scores relative to a query node for Sybil / synthetic-identity detection (Phase 7.5).

tools.name: graph.laundering_paths
tools.description: Enumerate all simple (cycle-free) directed fund-flow paths between source_id and target_id for AML / money-laundering investigations (Phase 7.5).

tools.name: graph.supply_chain_route
tools.description: Find the minimum-cost route between two nodes using multi-criteria A* search with optional edge cost_property and node heuristic_property (Phase 7.5).

cost_property.description: Edge property for cost (falls back to edge.weight).

heuristic_property.description: Node property for admissible heuristic h(n).

tools.name: graph.attack_paths
tools.description: Enumerate and rank cybersecurity attack paths from entry_node to asset_node scored by the product of per-edge exploitability weights in descending risk order (Phase 7.5).

tools.name: graph.recommend
tools.description: Generate collaborative-filtering item recommendations for user_node over bipartite user-item interaction edges (Phase 7.5).

user_node.description: User/entity node ID to generate recommendations for.

tools.name: graph.text_search
tools.description: Full-text BM25 / keyword search over graph nodes (zero embeddings or LLM required).  Returns policy-filtered matching nodes ranked by relevance score.

q.description: Search query string or node ID.

tools.name: graph.explain_query
tools.description: Return the Cost-Based Query Planner execution plan and selected strategy (PROPERTY_INDEX_SCAN, LABEL_INDEX_SCAN, VECTOR_SEARCH, TRAVERSAL, FULL_SCAN, HYBRID) for a Cypher query without executing it.

tools.name: graph.edges_count
tools.description: Return the total number of edges in the graph (the edge counterpart to graph.counts).

tools.name: graph.add_nodes_bulk
tools.description: Batch-insert up to 1,000 nodes in a single WAL-batched transaction (20x faster than individual graph.add_node calls).

tools.name: graph.add_edges_bulk
tools.description: Batch-insert up to 1,000 directed edges in a single WAL + Rayon batch (23.5x faster than individual graph.add_edge calls).

tools.name: graph.counts
tools.description: Return the total number of nodes in the graph, optionally filtered by label.  A cheap situational-awareness call an agent can make before deciding how to query or ingest.

label.description: Count only nodes with this label.  Omit for all nodes.

tools.name: graph.labels
tools.description: List every node type (label) in the graph with how many nodes carry it, largest first.  Cheap — O(types), not O(nodes).  Call this first to learn what the graph contains (e.g. Person, Account, Invoice) before querying or filtering by label.

tools.name: schema.get
tools.description: Return the full graph schema snapshot for the current tenant — all node-type and edge-type definitions plus constraints and version.  Call this first to discover the data model before querying or ingesting.

tools.name: schema.validate
tools.description: Validate the tenant's live graph data against the defined schema.  Reports missing required properties, type/enum violations, edge source/target-type violations, and orphan labels (labels present in the graph but undefined in the schema).  Returns valid=true with empty violation lists when the graph conforms.

tools.name: schema.list_node_types
tools.description: List every defined node type for the current tenant.

tools.name: schema.get_node_type
tools.description: Fetch a single node-type definition by its type_name.

tools.name: schema.define_node_type
tools.description: Define a new node type — the primitive that lets an agent build the data model itself.  The type_name becomes the canonical label for nodes of this type.  Set app_id to make the type a per-app IAM boundary (only matching API keys may touch its nodes).  Declare properties with per-field type / required / enum constraints, and immutable_properties that cannot change after creation.  Fails 409 if the type already exists (use schema.update_node_type to change).

app_id.description: Owning application ID — makes this type an app-level IAM boundary.  Omit for tenant-wide types.

data_classification.description: public | internal | restricted | highly_restricted.  Default internal.

properties.description: Map of property name → definition.  Each definition may set: type (string|str|integer|int|float|number|boolean|bool|datetime|list|array|dict|object), required (bool), description, enum (list of allowed values), default, indexed (bool).

required_labels.description: Additional labels every node of this type must carry.

immutable_properties.description: Properties that cannot be modified after node creation.

allowed_edge_types.description: Outgoing edge types this node type may participate in.  Omit for unrestricted.

tools.name: schema.update_node_type
tools.description: Update an existing node-type definition (full replace).  The type_name must match an existing type.  Does not migrate existing nodes — only the schema entry changes.  Fails 404 if the type is not defined.

type_name.description: Canonical node label — must match an existing type.

properties.description: Map of property name → definition.  Each definition may set: type (string|str|integer|int|float|number|boolean|bool|datetime|list|array|dict|object), required (bool), description, enum (list of allowed values), default, indexed (bool).

tools.name: schema.delete_node_type
tools.description: Remove a node-type definition.  Does NOT delete existing nodes — it only removes the schema entry, so nodes of this type become orphan-labelled until redefined.  ⚠ human_only — agents are blocked; a human operator must perform this action directly.

tools.name: schema.list_edge_types
tools.description: List every defined edge type for the current tenant.

tools.name: schema.get_edge_type
tools.description: Fetch a single edge-type definition by its type_name.

tools.name: schema.define_edge_type
tools.description: Define a new edge (relationship) type.  Constrain which node types may be the source/target, declare edge properties, and set cardinality (one_to_one | one_to_many | many_to_one | many_to_many).  Fails 409 if the type already exists.

source_node_types.description: Allowed source node types.  Omit for any.

target_node_types.description: Allowed target node types.  Omit for any.

properties.description: Map of property name → definition.  Each definition may set: type (string|str|integer|int|float|number|boolean|bool|datetime|list|array|dict|object), required (bool), description, enum (list of allowed values), default, indexed (bool).

cardinality.description: one_to_one | one_to_many | many_to_one | many_to_many.  Default many_to_many.

data_classification.description: public | internal | restricted | highly_restricted.  Default internal.

tools.name: schema.update_edge_type
tools.description: Update an existing edge-type definition (full replace).  The type_name must match an existing type.  Fails 404 if not defined.

type_name.description: Canonical edge type name — must match an existing type.

properties.description: Map of property name → definition.  Each definition may set: type (string|str|integer|int|float|number|boolean|bool|datetime|list|array|dict|object), required (bool), description, enum (list of allowed values), default, indexed (bool).

tools.name: schema.delete_edge_type
tools.description: Remove an edge-type definition.  Does NOT delete existing edges — only the schema entry is removed.  ⚠ human_only — agents are blocked; a human operator must perform this action directly.

tools.name: data.list_files
tools.description: List stored files in the current tenant's File Library with pagination.

tools.name: memory.history
tools.description: Retrieve the ordered message history for a session.  Use last_n to reconstruct the LLM context window on session resume.  Returns list of {seq, role, content, timestamp} dicts in ascending order.  Requires viewer role.

session_id.description: Session ID to retrieve history for.

last_n.description: Return only the last N turns.  Omit for full history.

tools.name: memory.search
tools.description: Semantic search across closed session summaries using vector similarity.  Returns the k most relevant past sessions for a given query.  Optionally filter by entity_id to scope to one user or agent.  This is the long-term memory recall path — query embeddings are compared against ChatSessionSummary nodes only (one per closed session).  Requires viewer role.

query.description: Natural-language query to find relevant past sessions.

entity_id.description: Scope search to sessions belonging to this entity.  Omit for global search.

k.description: Number of results to return.  Default 5.

tools.name: scheduler.add_trigger
tools.description: Register a temporal or event-driven trigger that fires an action.  Trigger types: 'interval' (every N seconds), 'cron' (5-field cron: 'm h dom mon dow'), or 'event' (a CDC event, optionally crossing a numeric threshold — this is how drift-crossing automations are built).  Action types: 'webhook' (HMAC-signed POST), 'emit_event' (chain a new CDC event onto the bus), or 'callback' (a named in-process handler such as starting/advancing a journey).  This is the time+condition entry point — no external scheduler needed.  Requires admin role.

interval_seconds.description: For trigger_type='interval': fire every N seconds.

event_type.description: For trigger_type='event': CDC event type to match (e.g. 'node_added', 'feedback_recorded').

condition.description: For event triggers: {field, op, value}, e.g. {'field':'data.drift','op':'ge','value':0.7}.

tenant_id.description: Restrict event triggers to one tenant.  Omit for all.

emit_event_type.description: For action_type='emit_event': CDC event type to publish.

payload.description: Static payload merged into the action body.

enabled.description: Whether the trigger is active.  Default true.

tools.name: scheduler.list_triggers
tools.description: List all registered trigger ids on the scheduler.  Requires admin role.

tools.name: scheduler.remove_trigger
tools.description: Unregister a trigger by id.  Idempotent.  Requires admin role.

tools.name: scheduler.status
tools.description: Return scheduler running state, all trigger specs, and fire/error counters.  Use to verify automations are live.  Requires admin role.

tools.name: egress.add_sink
tools.description: Register an outbound webhook sink that delivers graph change events (nodes/edges/journeys) to an external system as HMAC-signed JSON.  The mirror image of inbound connectors — this is how Purple8 pushes changes out to downstream systems in real time.  Optionally filter by event types and tenant, and reshape the payload with field mappings.  Requires admin role.

event_types.description: Only deliver these CDC event types (e.g. 'node_added', 'node_updated', 'edge_added', 'journey_started', 'stage_advanced', 'journey_completed', 'sla_breached', 'hitl_created', 'hitl_completed', 'feedback_recorded').  Omit for all.

tenant_id.description: Only deliver this tenant's events.  Omit for all.

tools.name: egress.list_sinks
tools.description: List all registered outbound sink ids.  Requires admin role.

tools.name: egress.remove_sink
tools.description: Unregister an outbound sink by id.  Idempotent.  Requires admin role.

tools.name: egress.status
tools.description: Return egress manager state, registered sinks, and delivery counters (delivered / failed / in-flight).  Requires admin role.

tools.name: feedback.record
tools.description: Record human or agent feedback about any graph entity — a RAG answer, a retrieved node, an inferred edge, or a journey.  Stored as an immutable graph record that flows through CDC (so egress sinks and scheduler drift-triggers can react) and feeds learning loops.  Give a rating, a label ('correct'/'incorrect'), a free-text comment, or a suggested correction.  Requires editor role.

target_id.description: Entity the feedback is about (node/edge/journey/answer id).

link_to_target.description: Also create a FEEDBACK_ON edge to the target node.  Default true.

tools.name: feedback.open
tools.description: List unresolved feedback items for this tenant (newest first).  The agent's work queue for acting on ground-truth signal.  Requires viewer role.

tools.name: feedback.summary
tools.description: Aggregate feedback signal for this tenant: total/resolved counts, mean rating, and label + kind tallies.  Use to gauge answer quality drift over time.  Requires viewer role.

tools.name: feedback.resolve
tools.description: Mark a feedback item as handled, recording how it was addressed (mirrors HITL resolution).  Emits a feedback_resolved CDC event.  Requires editor role.

tools.name: registry.register_tool
tools.description: Federate an EXTERNAL tool into this Purple8 gateway so every agent can call it alongside the built-in tools — Jira, a database HTTP API, Slack, a model endpoint, anything with an HTTP interface.  Purple8 holds the credential (envelope-encrypted) and proxies the call; the agent never sees the secret.  Give a namespaced name (e.g. 'jira.create_issue'), the transport ('rest' or 'mcp'), the base_url (SSRF-guarded), an optional credential and JSON input_schema, and the roles allowed to call it.  This is how the AI agent installs new capabilities for other agents.  Requires admin role.

transport.description: How to reach the tool: rest, mcp (downstream MCP server) or a2a (peer agent's A2A JSON-RPC URL).  Default 'rest'.

base_url.description: External https endpoint (passes the SSRF guard).

description.description: Human/agent-readable description of what the tool does.

method.description: HTTP method for rest transport.  Default 'POST'.

credential.description: {auth_type: none|bearer|api_key_header|basic, header_name, username, secret}.  Secret is encrypted at rest.

input_schema.description: JSON Schema for the tool's arguments (advertised to agents).

static_headers.description: Extra static headers sent on every call.

required_roles.description: Roles allowed to invoke.  Default editor+admin+super_admin.

tools.name: registry.register_mcp_server
tools.description: Federate a whole downstream MCP server (any Model / IDE / Bedrock / vendor MCP endpoint that speaks JSON-RPC 2.0).  Purple8 calls tools/list on it and registers EVERY advertised tool under '{prefix}.{tool}', so a single call imports an entire external toolbelt.  This is how any model or IDE 'registers itself' into the gateway.  Requires admin role.

prefix.description: Namespace prefix for the imported tools, e.g. 'bedrock'.

credential.description: Optional auth for the downstream server.

required_roles.description: Roles allowed to invoke the imported tools.

tools.name: registry.register_a2a_agent
tools.description: Federate a peer AI agent that speaks the A2A (Agent2Agent) protocol.  Purple8 fetches its Agent Card and registers one tool per advertised skill as '{prefix}.{skill_id}'.  Calling such a tool delegates a task to the remote agent (args: message, optional data / skill / arguments / task_id / context_id) and returns {state, text, artifacts, task_id}.  Requires admin role.

prefix.description: Namespace prefix for the agent's skills, e.g. 'billing_agent'.

card_url.description: Agent Card URL or the agent's base URL (SSRF-guarded).

credential.description: Optional auth for the peer: {auth_type: none|bearer|api_key_header|basic, header_name, username, secret}.

required_roles.description: Roles allowed to invoke the imported skills.

timeout_s.description: Max seconds to wait for a remote task.  Default 60.

tools.name: sentinel.list_findings
tools.description: List Sentinel findings — data drift, SOC threshold proposals, emerging threats — most severe first.  Each finding carries evidence, a DecisionGate trace and a proposed change awaiting HUMAN approval.  Agents cannot approve; surface open findings to the operator.

tools.name: sentinel.get_finding
tools.description: Fetch one Sentinel finding with full evidence, gate trace and proposal.

tools.name: sentinel.summary
tools.description: Counts of Sentinel findings by status, source and severity.

tools.name: sentinel.reject
tools.description: Dismiss an open Sentinel finding as noise, with a note.  (Approval is human-only and not available to agents.)

tools.name: sentinel.drift_check
tools.description: Compare current data against a stored baseline.  kind=distribution (values, PSI), embeddings (vectors, centroid shift) or quality (score, e.g. RAG F1).  Significant drift opens a finding for human review.

tools.name: evolution.routing_policy

Optimises quality − cost_weight×cost.  Never applies: an improvement opens a Sentinel finding a human must approve.

tools.name: evolution.rag_retrieval

An improvement opens a Sentinel finding; on human approval it is saved as collection profile profile_name.

tools.name: evolution.create_experiment

Then loop evolution.suggest → use config → evolution.report.

tools.name: guardrails.evaluate
tools.description: Run Purple8 AI guardrail checks on a text payload before writing it to the graph or passing it to an LLM.  Checks for prompt injection, scope escape, PII, token bombing, credential leaks (input); schema violations, credential leaks, and toxic content (output); and agent loop / cost runaway (structural).  Returns a GuardrailResult with passed, blocked, and a list of violations — each with guard name, severity (warn/flag/block), message, and evidence snippet.  REQUIRED: text (the payload to scan), check_type ('input'|'output'|'structural'). OPTIONAL: source_context (for hallucination probe), expected_schema (JSON Schema object for schema-violation check), call_stack (list of tool names for loop detection), total_tokens / retry_count / elapsed_s (for cost runaway). Agents SHOULD call this before data.ingest_text / data.ingest_file to catch prompt injection and credential leaks in user-supplied documents.

source_context.description: Source context for hallucination probe (output check only).

expected_schema.description: JSON Schema to validate LLM output against (output check only).

call_stack.description: Agent call-stack for loop detection (structural check).

total_tokens.description: Cumulative tokens consumed so far (structural check).

retry_count.description: Number of retries so far (structural check).

elapsed_s.description: Elapsed seconds for the pipeline run (structural check).

tools.name: admin.smtp_status
tools.description: Return the current outbound email (SMTP) configuration status for this Purple8 instance.  Shows whether SMTP is active, the host, port, and FROM address.  The password is never returned.  Call this first to check whether email (password-reset, user-invite) is already configured before prompting the operator for credentials.  Requires admin+.

tools.name: admin.smtp_configure
tools.description:
Configure outbound SMTP for this Purple8 instance so that password-reset and user-invite emails work.  HITL REQUIRED — you MUST ask the human operator for the SMTP credentials before calling this tool.  Never invent, guess, or reuse credentials from memory.  Present a form or prompt with: SMTP host, port (default 587), username, password, and optional from_name / from_address.  Only call this tool once the operator has explicitly provided all values.

Settings take effect immediately for the running process.  Remind the operator to add EMAIL__SMTP_HOST / EMAIL__SMTP_USER / EMAIL__SMTP_PASSWORD / EMAIL__SMTP_PORT to their .env or Docker environment to persist across restarts.  Requires admin+.

host.description: SMTP hostname, e.g. smtp.postmarkapp.com or smtp.gmail.com

port.description: SMTP port — 587 for STARTTLS (default), 465 for SSL

username.description: SMTP username — usually the full FROM email address

password.description: SMTP password or app-password (obtain from the operator via HITL)

from_name.description: Display name for outbound emails, e.g. 'Acme Platform'

from_address.description: FROM address (defaults to username if omitted)
